name: Ahiezer
overview: Ahiezer was a male leader from the tribe of Dan, serving as the head of his tribe during the census taken in the wilderness. He held a significant leadership role during the Exodus, guiding the people of Dan in this formative period of Israel's journey. His position as tribal head highlights his responsibility and authority within the camp of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahiezer means '[my] brother is a help,' reflecting a meaning rooted in familial support and assistance. This proper name, recorded in Numbers 1:12, does not indicate that it was given directly by God but carries a meaningful Hebrew significance.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Ahiezer was the son of Ammishaddai, establishing his lineage within the tribe of Dan. Beyond this father-son relationship, no additional family connections are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Ahiezer's role as the head of the tribe of Dan during the census signifies his leadership in organizing and representing his tribe during a critical moment of Israel's wilderness experience. His leadership contributed to the orderly arrangement and numbering of the people, which was essential for their military and communal structure. This underscores the importance of faithful stewardship and responsibility among God's appointed leaders during the Exodus.
